description:
## Problem
In BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot, downstream/delivery.py delivers a version only from the first-parent main commit that introduced it, and only after the three required push workflows succeeded at that commit. On 2026-11-25 a GitHub incident during the merge of PR #155 left merge commit e015509a (version 30.35.0.2) with no push-event runs. No rerun or dispatch can create a push run, so 30.35.0.2 can never be delivered. The recovery used was a version-only PR (#156, 30.35.0.3, merge a27947de) carrying the same source. downstream/MAINTAINING.md does not describe this failure or its recovery, and the stranded version stays in history.

## Change
Document the failure and the version-bump recovery in downstream/MAINTAINING.md, including how to confirm the missing push runs (gh run list -c <sha>) and that the stranded version is never delivered.

## Decision gates
- G1: the owner chooses documentation only (recommended) or a tooling change that lets delivery accept a later same-source commit. A tooling change weakens the source-commit rule and needs its own design review before code.

## Verification rubric
Pass only if: MAINTAINING.md describes the symptom, the check and the recovery, citing the 2026-11-25 case; if G1 chose tooling, a delivery test covers a stranded source commit and the existing source-commit tests still pass.

## Guardrails
- Fork rules apply: linked worktree from origin/main, the fork's review and merge process, never rewrite consumed main commits or tags.
- No change to the delivery gate's required-check rules without G1.
- Pinned human identity, no agent attribution.
